source: Telugu Voice Data Collection Tracker (Google Sheets)

categories.name: Places
categories.description: Houses, rooms, towns and the places between them.

categories.name: Animals
categories.description: Creatures named from daily life rather than from a book.

categories.name: Abstract
categories.description: Ideas with no physical form — the hardest words to borrow.

categories.name: Pronouns
categories.description: I, you, this, that. Small words that reveal grammar.

categories.name: Prepositions
categories.description: Words that place one thing against another.

categories.name: Relations
categories.description: Kinship terms — usually the most distinct vocabulary.

categories.name: Time
categories.description: Days, seasons and the words for when.

categories.name: Numbers
categories.description: Counting, where borrowing from Telugu is most likely.

categories.name: Sentences
categories.description: Whole utterances rather than single words.

words.en: This is a very good book.
Elder brother is reading a book.
Elder sister is listening to a song.
There is a book on the table.
There is a cat under the chair.
There is a tree in front of the house.
There is a shop near the school.
The dog is outside the house.
Children are playing in the park.
The bus is coming on the road.
The bird is on the tree.
I like this work very much.
She wakes up early in the morning.
We go to the park every Sunday.

words.te: మా ఇంటి దగ్గర ఒక ఆసుపత్రి ఉంది.
words.translit: Maa Inti Daggar Oka Aasupatri Undi.
words.en: There is a hospital near our house.
I have a lot of work today.
If it rains, I will stay at home.

words.te: నాకు ఆకలిగా ఉంది, కాబట్టి నేను భోజనం చేస్తున్నాను.
words.translit: Naaku Aakaligaa Undi, Kaabatti Nenu Bhojanam Chestunnaanu.
words.en: I am hungry, so I am eating.
He is tired, but he is working.
Let us do something good together.
